Level 3 · Advanced · Week 5

Sorting, Stacks and Queues

Sorting puts data in order; a stack remembers what to undo; a queue makes sure everyone gets a turn.

What you will learn

  • Sort a list with bubble sort and selection sort, and count the swaps.
  • Sort a leaderboard with sorted(key=..., reverse=True).
  • Use a stack to undo, and a queue to take turns.

Two ways to sort

Selection sort: find the smallest item and swap it to the front. Then find the smallest of the rest and swap it into second place. Repeat.
Bubble sort: walk along the list comparing neighbors. If the left one is bigger, swap them. After each pass the biggest item has “bubbled” to the end.

Python’s own sort

Python can sort for you. The key is a function that says what to sort by:

scores = [("Ada", 120), ("Leo", 95), ("Mei", 150)]

def points_of(entry):
    return entry[1]                  # sort by the number

best_first = sorted(scores, key=points_of, reverse=True)
print(best_first)   # [('Mei', 150), ('Ada', 120), ('Leo', 95)]

sorted makes a new list and leaves the old one alone.

Stacks and queues

A stack is like a pile of plates: you can only take the top one. “Undo” uses a stack: the last thing you did is the first thing undone. A queue is like a lunch line: join at the back, leave from the front. In Python, collections.deque is a fast queue.

Exercise5.1: Sort Race

Folder: week05/ex-sort-race. selection_sort is done. Finish the swap inside bubble_sort:

if result[i] > result[i + 1]:
    # swap both at once:
    result[i], result[i + 1] = result[i + 1], result[i]
    swaps = swaps + 1

Swaps for the 8 cards: selection (blank to fill in) bubble (blank to fill in)

Exercise5.2: Leaderboard

Folder: week05/ex-leaderboard. Finish name_of (sort A to Z, ignoring capitals), top_scores and the fair tie rule in rank_lines: equal points share a place, so the board reads 1, 2, 3, 3, 5.

Exercise5.3: Undo Paint

Folder: week05/ex-undo-paint. Finish the Stack class: push, pop, peek and size. Then run it, click the window, draw with the arrow keys and press u to undo. Each stroke is one item on the stack.

TipKind leaderboards

A good leaderboard uses nicknames, lets ties share a place, and celebrates personal bests and “most improved”, not only the winner.

Reflect

Where do you see a stack and a queue in real life or in apps you use?

Why is “undo” a stack and not a queue?

New words

sort
Put items in order, for example smallest to largest.
swap
Two items change places.
key function
A function that tells sorted what to sort by.
stack
A collection where the last item in is the first out (push and pop).
queue
A collection where the first item in is the first out (join at the back, leave at the front).
deque
Python’s fast queue, from collections . Say “deck”.

Homework: Sorting, Stacks and Queues

15–20 minutes. Do Core first; Challenge and Creative are optional.

CoreTurn Queue (about 10 minutes)

Four friends share one game. A queue makes it fair: the player at the front plays, then goes to the back of the line.

  1. Open week05/hw-turn-queue/starter.py in Thonny.

  2. Finish take_turn: player = queue.popleft(), then queue.append(player), then return the player.

  3. Finish leave: remove a player who has to go home, and return True (or False if they were not in the queue).

Predict: the queue is Priya, Sam, Kai, Zoe. Who plays turns 1 to 6? (blank to fill in)

ChallengeStack or queue?

Write S (stack) or Q (queue) next to each one, and say why in a few words.

Situation S or Q Why
The back button in a web browser
Songs waiting in a playlist
Printing 3 documents sent one after another
A pile of homework sheets, newest on top

CreativeDesign a fair leaderboard

Sketch a leaderboard screen for a game you like. Use nicknames only. Include at least one thing that celebrates effort, not only winning (for example “most improved”, “personal best”, or “longest streak of helping”).
